Self-Adapting Video World Models at Test Time

NARRA adapts a video world model to its own rollout at test time, keeping scenes consistent over minute-long camera paths.

Paula Arguello1 Ali Behrouz2 Vahab Mirrokni2 Mahdi Soltanolkotabi1,2

1 2Research

Highlight Method 60 s results vs. backbone 16 s results Baselines BibTeX

Video world models drift over long rollouts: when the camera returns to a place it has already seen, the scene has changed.

Proposed Method

NARRA treats its first rollout as self-supervised data and adapts part of the model before the final generation.

60-Second Results

Each clip is a single uninterrupted 60-second rollout (960 frames, 16 fps).

Comparison with the Backbone (60 s)

Same scene and camera path. Left: backbone context. Right: NARRA.

16-Second Results

Shorter rollouts across indoor, outdoor and stylized scenes.

Comparison with World-Model Baselines (16 s)

Top: backbone context and NARRA. Bottom: DreamX-World, ReWorld and WorldPlay.
